simplified: Your dreams can give you ideas about things you didn't know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing your teeth, or being naked in public, usually mean similar things for many people. But to really understand what they mean for you, you need to link them to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

One interesting case of wild animals living in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. There are about 35,000 wild dogs on the streets of Moscow. Some dogs were born wild, and some were pets that their owners left behind. Some dogs live alone, while others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied these dogs and found that they have adapted very well to city life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs seem to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is RJ Palacio's first book. She says on her website that she got the idea for the story after seeing a girl with a facial difference on the street. The book has sold a lot of copies in the United States and has won many awards. Many schools are using it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is being made, and many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe has two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows they are not usual pets, and she has tried many times to explain that rats are not dirty and can be great pets if cared for properly. She understands why people might not like them. She didn't like rats at first until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how friendly and smart they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to have two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have been shocked by electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce problems with people, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to chase baboons out of the city or catch them and release them in the countryside. This plan has worked a bit, but it is hard to stop baboons from returning to the city because they find easy food there.

I work for a big IT company, but their main office is in the United States, so I do my job online from home. This way, I don’t waste time traveling or talking with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this flexibility is important to me because I can take time off when my kids have school events or if I need to see the dentist. The downside is that without set working hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.

In the 1990s, graffiti was still popular, but street art also grew a lot around the world. Some artists wanted to share political messages about war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists focused on making beautiful art. In South America, many street artists worked in poor areas to add color and beauty to dull city walls.

Social media, magazines, and store displays show people many things to buy, and British shoppers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people can use a few times and then throw away.

Sam squinted at the sun and saw the dust from the car going to the Big House. The horses were swatting flies and didn’t care that their owner was visiting after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter only came out when he needed to, which was good for Sam. The more he stayed away from his boss, the longer he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. The wet spots on his shirt looked like shapes on a map. His skin was already getting red in the June sun. He looked like a man who made money while others worked.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs was too cruel, and there were strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council decided to take a more peaceful approach. Instead of shooting the pigs, they built fences and made it illegal to feed them. We will see if this plan works, but it might be hard because warmer winters mean there are more pigs now.

A big inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of Greek myths. When she was a child, one of her favorite stories was about Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, Athens is controlled by Crete, but the people of Athens fight back. As a punishment, the king of Crete, Minos, makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The young people are put into a maze and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. But one boy, named Theseus, fights and kills the Minotaur. Suzanne thinks of Katniss Everdeen as a modern Theseus.

Zoos can teach people about protecting animals and their homes by bringing people and animals together. Some zoos help animals that were hurt in circuses or pets that were left behind. They also do important research on how animals behave and how to help them when they are sick.

A new trend is starting against buying too much – the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the early 1990s and then came to the US, where it is against spending too much on Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving. On Buy Nothing Day, people do different protests and cut their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups help people exchange and fix things they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on how you see it, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is seen as vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils say it costs a lot to clean graffiti off buildings, buses, and trains.

What do people in the art world think about graffiti and street art? More and more people are starting to see it as real art. There have been big shows of street art in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, the American artist Elura Emerald organized a street art show in a New York gallery. She supported street artists by saying, "Artists who paint on the street are just expressing themselves and not hurting anyone. They should be appreciated."

Most people have four to six dreams every night after they turn ten, which means they can have about 2,000 dreams each year. By the time someone is 80 years old, they might have had around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget most of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand throughout our lives. It’s easy to think that sometimes a dream can be similar to something that happens in real life, especially if the dream is about something common.

The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America was destroyed. The country is called Panem and has twelve poor areas controlled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol has all the power. Each area makes different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth area, but it was destroyed because it rebelled against the Capitol.

Wild animals sometimes come into cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started going into neighborhoods to eat. They open trash bins and take fruit from gardens. Some bold baboons have even entered people's homes and taken food from kitchens! Baboons can be dangerous and have hurt many pets, so many people in the city do not like them.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because the engineers make mistakes, like calculating wrong. The bridge can fall down, which can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the first movie directors to base his story on the 17 steps of the hero's journey. Usually, the hero starts with a normal life, but then something happens that leads them to an adventure that changes everything. At the start of Star Wars, Luke has a normal life with his aunt and uncle, fixing robots. When he discovers Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi in the robot R2D2, it is the moment that calls him to adventure and begins his journey.

Another idea to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to blow it up with a nuclear bomb. It sounds like a movie plot, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real plan from NASA. The rockets, which weigh eight tons, would be shot at an asteroid to try to change its path. If the asteroid is too close for this to work, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to blow it up.

Campbell says that the hero first does not want to go on an adventure, but then a mentor helps them, and they decide to enter a special world where the adventure takes place. In this stage, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to prepare for their biggest challenge. For Luke, the mentor is Obi-Wan, the friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and the enemy is Darth Vader in the special world of the Death Star.

Some things that are not used much might seem useless to some people, but others can find them useful. With the internet, online groups have found ways to make money by sharing these items. Now, it is easier to buy and sell second-hand things through websites and social media. This is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we don't know about ourselves. Freud thought that if we understand our dreams, we can learn about our hidden feelings and problems. The other idea was different. It said that dreams are just random thoughts in our brain while it organizes memories from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and make a story from them.

I work for myself as a freelancer. This is good because I can choose what I do and how I use my time. At first, I worked from home, but it was hard to focus because there were many distractions, like housework, tea, and family members needing my help. So, I tried working at a café, but the Wi-Fi was not good, and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I decided to rent a desk in a shared office with five other freelancers. I liked getting ready for work in the morning and being able to concentrate in an office.

NASA needs money to build a special telescope called NEOCam, which will help find middle-sized asteroids. If they get the money, they could reach their goal in ten years. After finding the asteroids, the team will still need to figure out how to protect the planet from the dangerous ones.

The 'buy nothing' trend is now popular with social media influencers who usually post about clothes and make-up to buy. Some YouTube stars tell their viewers not to buy anything for up to a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year only buying food. In the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or home items. In the next stage, they stopped using services like haircuts, eating at restaurants, or buying gas for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

Pi cares about religion. His family is Hindu, but he is interested in other religions too. He becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi says he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers ask him to pick one religion, Pi says, "I just want to love God." After that, his family and teachers let him decide about religion on his own.

Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have clearer dreams. In lucid dreams, you know you are dreaming and can change what happens in the dream. This means you could turn a scary dream into a nice one or control the story of your dream like a movie director. Instead of just figuring out what your dreams mean, you will be making them, but you might still want some dreams that let your mind share its thoughts!

Some people may not know they are part of the problem with cheap clothes because they give their old clothes to charities. But charity shops cannot sell all those old clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of style quickly and is often too low quality to recycle; people do not want to buy it used. A lot of it gets thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, which creates more economic and environmental issues.

Some adventurers want more than one great trip. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountains, biked across Canada, and run a long race in the Sahara Desert in very hot weather. But her most amazing trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help to get out. Many people would have stopped there, but Meagan chose to keep going. She reached the South Pole forty days later, pulling a sled with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.

Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls of Paris. Now, he wants people to think about social issues. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to make residents think about homelessness.

In some places, local governments have tried to help artists by giving them special areas to paint instead of letting them paint anywhere. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can paint on walls. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city has even let some artists paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints large, colorful pictures of people and animals and enjoys exploring different places. You can find her art on sidewalks, in empty factories, and on old cars. She likes that most street art does not last long and will be washed away by rain or cleaned up by city workers. For her, this shows how life is always changing with its endings and new beginnings.

In her last job, Gabriela worked in a culture where people respect power and authority, and everyone knows their place. In that culture, leaders make the important decisions and are rarely questioned. However, her Swedish team was used to a culture where employees often work with their bosses to solve problems and make decisions. In this culture, leaders help and encourage independent thinking and expect to be challenged.

When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences between her and her team, she decided to talk openly with them about how they felt about her leadership. Her team was happy to share their thoughts and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom to be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she didn't trust them to do their jobs well. They understood that Gabriela took it personally when they tried to suggest changes to her decisions, and they explained that it was just how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos são irmãos gêmeos idênticos de São Paulo. Eles pintam desde pequenas marcas até grandes e coloridas imagens de pessoas nas paredes dos prédios. Seu trabalho é tão grande que eles precisam de guindastes para ajudar. Em 2007, eles pintaram todo um castelo na Escócia.

People have painted and written on walls for a long time. In ancient times, people in Africa and Europe painted pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin. These include messages about religion, politics, love, and even some magic spells!

Have you ever wanted to climb Mount Everest or walk to the South Pole? If yes, you are not the only one. Every year, many people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across countries. Unlike explorers in the past who used maps, today’s adventurers use technology like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and travel to raise awareness about environmental problems, while others want to help people and raise money for charities.

The first test is called DART, which stands for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. They plan to test DART on a moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, called 'Didymoon,' is 150 meters wide and goes around its bigger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that DART will hit it and change its path so that telescopes on Earth can see it.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. She lost her father in a mining accident and needs to find food for her family. She hunts in the woods near District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very good with a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is chosen to compete, Katniss decides to go in her place. The other competitor from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss starts to have a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details. Think about the people and places in your dreams because they might be important too. After a week, you will be surprised by how much you have written. You can then connect your dreams to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.
In the past, many bridges were made of wood and could easily catch fire. This was especially true for old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could start a fire.

We cannot know how street art will change in the future, but we see some trends. Most street artists are young people who paint in their cities, but more are traveling to work in different places. Some artists use the internet to connect and share pictures of their art. The art world is also starting to recognize street art as real art. Even though we don't know what will happen next, street art is definitely going to stay!

Suzanne Collines has always found news about wars upsetting. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to protect her by not telling her about the war, but she still saw news about it and knew her dad was there. It was very scary for her.

In a worldwide survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), over 40,000 young people and older people answered questions about work culture, communication, pay, career growth, and work-life balance. In another survey by Deloitte, more than 10,000 young people shared their views on the challenges and chances in today's work environment.

Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is an adventurer. He has ridden a bike in the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Erik has been blind since he was 13 years old. He also helps people with disabilities to be active and takes groups of young blind people climbing.

Online platforms are giving people a chance to make some extra money. For example, busy parents used to not sell their children's old things at local markets, but now they can sell baby clothes and equipment online to earn some cash.

Pi and Richard Parker stay in the lifeboat for 227 days. They face hunger, sickness, and tiredness. They go through strong storms and the hot sun, but they manage to survive. Sometimes, Pi feels comfort from his three religions, but other times he feels very lonely and sad. Finally, they see the Mexican coast, and everything changes. It would be a shame to tell you the ending, so you should read the book to find out what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.

Chloe came home from school, made a cup of coffee, and took it to her room. She had homework to do, but she wanted to relax first. She liked the quiet time before her parents got home and the house became noisy with talking, the TV, or her dad listening to jazz while cooking. She also enjoyed this time because she could play with her pet rats.

In 2010, NASA's team for protecting the planet found and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1 kilometer wide. These 'near-Earth objects' are very big, like mountains, and include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's path. NASA thinks there are about 50 more to find, but says that none of the 887 they know about are a big danger to Earth.

Auggie decides to go to school, but his first day is very scary. Like every new student, he feels nervous. Because of how he looks, it is really hard for him. No one wants to sit with him, and he sees other kids looking at him and whispering. Luckily, he makes friends with Jack and Summer. But the first day is not the only difficult time. Auggie finds out that his classmates don’t want to touch him because they are afraid of getting sick. Throughout the school year, Auggie has many ups and downs until a surprising and upsetting event at a school camp changes everything.

The two men looked at the northern side of the land. It went on for a long way, and they could hardly see the fences. Even if a bored teenage boy wanted to escape, he couldn't walk away. Sam watched the biggest horse, which was kicking the ground. He wondered if the boy could ride. A good rider could find trouble out there, far from anyone. But someone who didn't know about horses might get into even more trouble trying to run away from his father.

More than 4,000 climbers, between the ages of thirteen and eighty, have reached the top of Everest. Climbing high mountains in cold weather and strong storms is still very dangerous, but the best climbers in the world are now looking for new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria started to love mountain climbing when she was a teenager. After finishing school, she worked as a nurse but continued to climb in her free time.

After climbing Everest, Gerlinde chose to climb all fourteen of the world's tallest mountains. To make it harder, she climbs without oxygen tanks, which is dangerous because there is less oxygen at the top. Gerlinde uses her fame to help a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.

If we look at the things we have bought in our lives, we can see that not everything is used well: the warm coat we thought was stylish even though we live in a hot country, the old smartphone we stopped using when we got a new one, the car we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that has become a storage room.

Throughout history, many cultures believed that dreams could predict the future. People thought dreams were messages from the gods that gave us important information. Even now, many people remember dreaming about something that later happened in real life.

Some of the largest and most costly transportation projects in the world have included building bridges. Bridges are important connections that allow cars, trucks, and trains to cross water, mountains, or other roads.

After many weeks of problems, Gabriela wrote an email to her Swedish manager about the issues with her team. Her manager just asked if she thought her team was still doing well and what could help her work better with them. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and did not feel he was handling the situation well.

Dogs that live in groups have learned that people are more likely to give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to ask for food for the whole group. Some dogs have even learned to use the metro to move around their area! Scientists are not sure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of places they like. Another idea is that they understand the names of stations from the announcements. Either way, people on the metro have become used to seeing dogs on the trains, and they mostly ignore them.

Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk the whole Amazon River. He began at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and reached the river's end in Brazil after two years and four months, walking 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest has dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, so Ed was always in danger. Fortunately, he only got a lot of mosquito and ant bites.

In Britain, the average person spends more than £1,000 on new clothes each year, which is about four percent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two bigger problems for society and the environment. First, many people are using credit cards to pay for these clothes. British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of what they spend on clothes. Also, people are buying things they don’t need and spending money they don’t have. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing every year, and most of it ends up in landfills.

Ed's walk would not have been possible without technology. He used a radio to ask people in the rainforest for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to help him and guide him through hard areas. While walking, Ed wrote a blog about his daily experiences. He used the media attention from his trip to talk about the destruction of the rainforest and to raise money for charities that help the environment and children in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have realized they can make money from the sharing economy by using resources that are not fully used. A popular business model involves companies creating online platforms that connect customers with people who offer specific products or services. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses for extra income. Another example is Uber, which allows people to use their own cars as taxis to earn some extra money in their free time.

One important job of modern zoos is to help breed endangered animals from different countries. In the wild, some rare animals have trouble finding mates and having babies, and they can also be in danger from hunters, losing their homes, and other animals. A good zoo helps these animals live and breed safely. Also, as some wild animals become fewer, they can become too similar genetically. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild to make the gene pool more diverse.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can make a bridge fall for different reasons. Trains can bring down a bridge because they hit it very hard. Boats can cause a bridge to fall because they are very heavy, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to stop bridges from falling is to plan ahead. New technologies that find weak spots, safer work areas, and better designs can help reduce these accidents.

At first, Pi is very scared of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water and knows he must climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other until only Pi and the tiger are left. Luckily for Pi, the tiger, which he names Richard Parker, feels sick and does not want to eat him right away.

When Pi is 16, a new government is chosen that his parents do not like. They are worried about the future, so they decide to close the zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family travels by ship to Canada with the animals. During the journey, a big storm happens, and the ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi ends up in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a big tiger.

The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teenagers and young adults by the American writer Suzanne Collins. Since it came out in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies worldwide. It was also the first book for young readers to sell over a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie and is very successful. It made 152.5 million dollars in its first weekend in North America!

Dreams might happen because our mind is sorting out the thoughts we have during the day, but they show up in dreams with special meanings. When we are awake, we usually think in words, like talking to ourselves. But when we sleep, the part of our brain that helps us use language is less active, while the part that deals with feelings is more active.

Having good relationships is very important for happiness. In one study, most happy people had strong connections with friends and family and spent time with them often. You also need at least one person to talk to about your feelings, which is called 'self-disclosure'. Just one close friend is enough, along with other relationships. It’s not enough to have many friends just to hang out or talk about music or football. That deeper connection is very important. Some people need to learn how to listen better to others to build stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck talked about how our brains can change and how we can get better at skills we weren't good at before. Many people often praise the final results and natural talents, like saying, "You are great at noticing details" or "You are really good at organizing events." But research shows that if we focus on how things are done—like praising effort, trying new things, and solving problems—we can help people learn new skills and improve their talents.

The rover checks the air around it from time to time, and in 2014 it discovered that the air had methane, which is a simple organic molecule and an important part of natural gas. Methane only lasts for a few hundred years, so something on Mars must be making more of it. NASA says Mars releases thousands of tons of methane at once, and the amount of methane goes up and down with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

Early in her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-olds some problems that were a bit too hard for them. One group liked the challenge and believed they could get better. She called this a 'growth mindset' because they thought about what they could achieve in the future. But another group felt like their intelligence was being judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and couldn’t see how they could improve. Some of these children said they might cheat later; others looked for someone who did worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films like empty places. This could be an old hospital, a scary empty house, or a ghost town. There is something about lonely places. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they leave? It is also very quiet, which can be scary. Abandoned places are good for horror films because there is usually no phone signal there.

No matter what type of house it is, the basement is a scary place in horror movies. It's usually where something is hiding or where the bad person keeps their tools. Basements are dark and often wet. You can only get to them by a small staircase. Basements are always creepy, even if there is nothing there.

Gary Collins, a policeman who was not working, was watching the London riots on TV. He saw some people he knew and decided to end his holiday early to help identify them. He spent six months looking at CCTV footage and identified 190 people, often just by their eyes. His help was very important for the investigation. Even though there were 200,000 hours of video, the facial recognition software only found one person.

I find it interesting to think about how we can make our bodies better. Imagine if we could put a computer in our brain! Soon, we will be able to do this and improve our math skills, how we see and hear, and our memory. This idea will become more normal.

The talk was interesting, and the speaker made some good points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework when they see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting at a stoplight? She also mentioned that people want to be in many places at once, so they switch between real-life and online chats. I notice this with my teenage daughter and her friends. They meet up but often sit quietly while talking to others online.

There are news stories that make us think the world is more violent, but there is also some good news. From the end of World War II to 1990, there were 30 wars that killed over 100,000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but countries are mostly living together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. Still, the news is not all bad. Even though violent crime is nine times more likely to cause deaths than political conflict, the global murder rate went down a little, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has spent her life helping human rights and has seen many projects in her country to teach women and girls. However, when these projects end, the women are often left with nothing. She realized that Bangladesh needed to be stronger, so she combined her love for climbing and human rights to change how people think about women in her country. She started climbing while working on projects in Tibet and Nepal because most people in flat Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working, and people in her country and around the world are starting to pay attention.

Most people think that developing countries are very poor and have bad leaders, with no chance for change. But this is not true. In fact, many good things are happening. In the last 20 years, over 700 million people have earned more money and left poverty. Also, six million fewer children die from sickness each year, more girls are going to school, and many people have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback nicer by putting a positive comment before and after a negative one. But if they do this all the time, workers might think the positive comments are just hiding the bad news, which makes them less valuable. Positive feedback should not just cover up the negative but should help encourage good work.

I am part of a group that wants to stop dangerous robots. Forget about the scary robots in movies. Right now, military machines like drones and robots are already being used to kill people with little help from humans. The next step will be robots that can decide who to kill by themselves. I believe this is very wrong and could be dangerous for everyone. We need to be careful about what we let machines do.

More people are learning English than all the other languages together, and English is spoken in the most countries. However, Chinese has the most native speakers. There is not much connection between the number of native speakers and the number of learners, but there is a stronger connection between the number of learners and how many countries speak the language.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about your work on the recent project. You worry all weekend about what you might have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by saying nice things about your work, and you think this is how she usually gives feedback. You know she will say something good, then tell you what needs to improve, and then say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a fast rock album with catchy songs, but its lyrics are very emotional. The songs tell stories about the struggles of regular people who work hard but do not get rich or famous. For example, the song Glory Days is about people in a small town remembering their youth, while Downbound Train is about a young man who loses his job and feels lost. The artist seems to share real stories from his life and the lives of people he knows. This album shows how talented the artist is.

Lewis wants the number of protected ocean areas to go up from 3 percent to 10 percent to help fix the damage caused by things like overfishing and pollution. He has seen this damage himself during his trips. He has swum over coral reefs that have lost their color because the water is too warm and has seen empty areas in the Red Sea filled with plastic. Lewis believes that nature can heal if we give it a chance, but we need to act quickly. If we don’t take care of our oceans, we might face a big problem soon.

Best-selling author Terrie Sharp knows how to tell good stories. She has won the Olive Crime Writer Award two times. She grew up in a place in Glasgow with a lot of crime, where she learned to be quiet and stay safe. She also learned how to open car doors with a knife, but she only used this skill for her books. Now, she talks more and appears on popular daytime shows and at writing events in the UK.

Are things getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker talks about human progress and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, and happier lives. The real problem, Pinker says, is that the values of reason and science are being attacked. When people focus on tribalism and distrust, we risk harming important things like democracy and working together in the world.

In old horror movies, when the main characters were in trouble, it was hard or impossible for them to get help or call the police. Now, with mobile phones, that seems less real. To keep the suspense, there is often no phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror movie, it is very likely that when you really need to call for help, you won’t have any signal. Or your phone battery will die right when you try to call. Or both.

In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America were losing their best product, the Gros Michel banana, also called Big Mike. Now, the same thing is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish banana. The Gros Michel banana was popular because it was easy to transport and had a thick skin and sweet taste. United Fruit, the main banana grower and exporter in South America at that time, produced bananas very efficiently by cloning parts of the plants instead of using seeds and growing them close together in fields.

Most spiders have venom that helps them catch their food, not to hurt people. Only 25 types of spiders can harm humans, and while their bites can hurt, they usually are not deadly. The Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia has not killed anyone since they made an anti-venom in 1981. But be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel scared, they can shoot out irritating hairs to protect themselves.

This scary movie idea was very popular in horror films from the late 1900s. It begins with a group of teenagers having fun, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At first, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she becomes the strongest and smartest person. The last girl usually wins.

If we want to understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to look at how our brains are different from other animals. It's not just about brain size; it's also important to know what else our brains can do and why they changed over time. There are not many physical clues to help us; things left by our ancestors don't show us what kind of speech they could make. However, we can see that early humans had changes in their mouth, throat, and tongue. By around 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds. Before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

Society tells us that girls should like arts and humanities, while boys should do maths and physics. There are not many positive female role models in science jobs. Cartoons and stories often show scientists as men. People also think that scientists are strange and not good at socializing, which is not true. These ideas can make girls feel like they don’t belong in science and see it as a boring career. If girls saw more successful women in science, it would help them feel more confident and included.

The Scallion is a free newspaper that comes out every week and is given out in faculty buildings. About 10,000 students read it. It is made by students. A survey shows that university students and staff really like the newspaper for fun, culture, and work experience. Printing the newspapers costs a lot of money. Also, some students find it hard to get a copy because they have to go to the university to pick one up. Another problem is that many copies become litter on campus.

At Girox Foods, about 12 out of every 100 employees leave each year. This number seems high because the usual rate in the industry is 7 out of 100. This report aims to find out why employees feel engaged at work and to suggest ways to make their experience better and keep them longer.

The speaker said many true things. I really believe that being more connected can make us feel more alone. My generation, who lived without technology for a long time, knows how to be alone and that it's okay. But for those under 20, it's different. They talk a lot but don’t feel alone, which means they might not learn to enjoy being by themselves. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of having real conversations with people face to face.

Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If you always give both, people might not value the positive comments. Make sure to give positive feedback sometimes without adding criticism.

Your dreams can reveal insights about thoughts you weren't aware of. Common dreams, such as flying, falling, losing teeth, or being naked in public, often have similar meanings for many people. However, to truly understand what these dreams mean for you, it's important to connect them to your daily experiences and emotions.

One of the most fascinating examples of wild animals living in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. Approximately 35,000 wild dogs roam the streets of Moscow. Some of these dogs were born in the wild, while others were once pets that were abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone, while others form packs. In 2010, scientists conducted a study on these dogs and discovered that they have adapted very well to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs even seem to understand how traffic lights work.

"Wonder is the first novel by RJ Palacio. On her website, she shares that the idea for the book came to her after she saw a girl with facial deformities on the street. The book has become a bestseller in the United States and has received several awards. Many schools are using it to start conversations about bullying, friendship, and what it means to be different. A film adaptation is in the works, and many people, including myself, are looking forward to seeing what RJ Palacio will write next."

Chloe owns two pet rats called Zena and Roxy. She realizes they are not common pets, and she has often tried to explain that rats are not dirty and can be wonderful pets if taken care of properly. She understands why some people have a negative reaction. She also didn't like rats until her friend Martin introduced her to his pet rats, and she noticed how affectionate and intelligent they could be. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to adopt two of them.

Cape Town can be a risky place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents, while others have been electrocuted when they played with electric cables. Since baboons are an endangered species, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors to help protect them and reduce conflicts with humans. The monitors are responsible for chasing baboons out of urban areas or capturing them and releasing them in the countryside. This approach has had some success, but it is challenging to prevent baboons from returning to the city once they discover it offers easy food.

I work for a global IT company, but since their headquarters is in the United States, I do all my work online from home. This means I don’t waste time commuting or chatting with colleagues. I work on various projects, and this flexibility is very important to me because I can easily take time off for my children’s school performances or dentist appointments. However, the downside is that without clear office hours, I often end up working late into the evening and sometimes skip dinner to complete my tasks.

In the 1990s, graffiti remained popular, but there was also a significant rise in street art globally. Some artists aimed to express political ideas and created art that encouraged people to think about issues like war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists were more focused on creating beautiful and appealing works. In South America, many street artists worked in impoverished neighborhoods, bringing color, life, and beauty to grey city walls.

Social media, magazines, and shop windows constantly show people things to buy, and British consumers are purchasing more clothes and shoes than ever before. Online shopping allows customers to buy things easily without much thought, while major brands sell such inexpensive clothes that they can be treated as disposable items, worn a few times and then discarded.

Sam squinted against the sun as he watched the dust trail from the car heading to the Big House. The horses kicked and swatted at flies, not caring that their owner was visiting for the first time in ten months. Sam waited patiently. Mr. Carter only came out when necessary, which suited Sam just fine. The more he stayed out of his boss's way, the longer he would keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped the sweat from his neck, and the damp patches on his shirt formed shapes like those on a map. His skin was already turning red from the June sun, and he had the tan of a man who made money while others did the work.

Many residents in Berlin, Germany, complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel, leading to heated arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council chose to take a more peaceful approach. Instead of shooting the pigs, they built fences and made it illegal to feed them. It remains to be seen if this strategy will be effective, but it could be a difficult challenge since warmer winters have led to an increase in pig populations.

A significant inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's passion for classical Greek mythology. As a child, one of her favorite stories was about Theseus and the Minotaur. In this tale, the city of Athens is under the control of Crete, but the Athenians rebel against this rule. As punishment, King Minos of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete each year. These youths are thrown into a labyrinth where a monster called the Minotaur lives, and they are eaten by it. However, one of the youths, named Theseus, bravely fights and kills the Minotaur. Suzanne views Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic version of Theseus.

By bringing people and animals together, zoos can educate the public about conservation and inspire them to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe place for animals that were mistreated in circuses or abandoned as pets. They also conduct important research on animal behavior and how to treat their illnesses.

A new trend is emerging that opposes consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and later spread to the US, where it rejects the excessive spending during Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, people organize protests and cut their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups facilitate the exchange and repair of items that people already own.

Is graffiti considered art or vandalism? This question depends on your perspective, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is viewed as vandalism. Many street artists have faced police action, and some have had to pay fines. City councils often complain about the high costs of removing graffiti from buildings, buses, and trains.

What is the opinion of the art world on graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been an increasing recognition of its value as an art form. Major exhibitions of street art have taken place in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, the American artist Elura Emerald organized a street art exhibition at a gallery in New York. She defended street artists by saying that they are simply expressing themselves and not causing harm. They deserve to be appreciated and celebrated.

Most people have four to six dreams each night after they turn ten, adding up to about 2,000 dreams a year. By the age of 80, the average person could have experienced around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 percent of them, we still remember a few thousand dreams in our lifetime. It’s not hard to believe that a dream might be followed by a similar event in real life, especially if the dream is about something that happens often in daily life.

The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America has been destroyed. The country is named Panem and consists of twelve poor districts that are ruled by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol has complete control over the nation. Each district produces different goods for the Capitol. The story begins in District 12, which supplies all the coal for the country. There was once a thirteenth district, but it rebelled against the Capitol in the past and was destroyed.

Wild animals often enter cities in search of food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun to invade residential areas to find something to eat. They open garbage bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some daring baboons have even gone into people's houses and taken food from kitchen cupboards and refrigerators! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked many pets, so it is understandable that many city residents do not welcome them.

A lot of accidents happen during bridge construction. These accidents are often caused by mistakes made by the engineers, such as miscalculations. When the bridge collapses under its own weight, it can be very dangerous for the workers who are on it at that moment.

George Lucas was one of the early film directors to base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically, the hero begins with an ordinary life, but an event occurs that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. In Star Wars, Luke lives a normal life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it serves as the call to adventure that starts him on his journey.

Another proposed way to defend against an asteroid heading towards Earth is to use a nuclear weapon to blow it up. While it may seem like a movie plot, as seen in the 1998 film Armageddon, the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real proposal from NASA. The plan involves firing eight-ton rockets at an approaching asteroid to try to change its course. If the asteroid is too close for this method to succeed, the rockets would be equipped with nuclear bombs to destroy it.

According to Campbell, the hero initially refuses the call to adventure, but then a mentor appears to help them, leading them to 'cross the threshold' into a special world where the adventure unfolds. The hero must then face tests, battle enemies, and meet friends as they prepare for their greatest challenge. In Luke's case, Obi-Wan is the mentor, Han Solo and the droids R2D2 and C3PO are his friends, and Darth Vader is the enemy within the special world of the Death Star.

Items that are not used much may seem worthless to some, but they can be valuable to others. With the rise of the internet, online communities have discovered how to profit from sharing these underused items. Thanks to websites and social media groups that help buy and sell second-hand goods, peer-to-peer sharing has become easier than ever. This concept is known as the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main theories about dreams became popular. One theory suggested that dreams represent things that are hidden from our conscious mind. Freud believed that by understanding our dreams, we could learn about our hidden feelings and the problems they create. The other theory was quite different; it claimed that dreams are simply random brain activity while we organize our memories and experiences from the day. When we wake up, we try to make sense of these random images and feelings and create a story from them.

I am a freelancer, which means I work for myself. This is great because I have control over my work and how I spend my time. At first, I worked from home, but I found it difficult to concentrate due to many distractions, like housework, wanting another cup of tea, and my family needing my attention. I then tried working at a nearby café, but the Wi-Fi connection was not very good, and I ended up drinking too much coffee. Eventually, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I enjoyed getting dressed for work in the morning and being able to focus in an office setting.

NASA's ability to find the remaining middle-sized asteroids depends on securing funding for NEOCam, a 0.5-meter space telescope that uses infrared light to detect asteroids. If they receive the funding, they could likely achieve this goal in ten years. Once they identify the asteroids, the planetary defense team will still need to determine how to protect Earth from the most concerning ones, known as PHAs.

The 'buy nothing' trend has become popular among social media influencers who typically share recommendations for clothing and make-up. Some YouTube stars now encourage their viewers to avoid buying anything for up to a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year focusing only on buying food. During the first three months, they learned to live without purchasing electronics, clothes, or household items. In the next phase, they stopped using services like haircuts, dining out, or buying petrol for their cars. By the end of the year, they had saved $55,000.

Religion is important to Pi. Although his family practices Hinduism, he is curious about other religions and makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi claims to be Hindu, Muslim, and Christian all at once. When his family and teachers ask him to choose only one religion, Pi refuses, saying, "I just want to love God." From that point on, his family and teachers allow him to make his own decisions about religion.

Some people think that writing down your dreams can help you experience lucid dreaming. Lucid dreams are when you realize you are dreaming and can make choices that change what happens in the dream. This means you could turn a nightmare into a pleasant dream or guide the story of your dream like a film director. So, instead of just figuring out what your dreams mean, you will be creating them, although you might still want to have some dreams that let your subconscious express what is on your mind!

Many people may not realize they contribute to the disposable clothing problem because they donate their unwanted clothes to charities. However, charity shops cannot sell all of those clothes. 'Fast fashion' quickly goes out of style and is often too low quality to recycle, so people do not want to buy it second-hand. A large amount ends up being thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent abroad, leading to more economic and environmental problems.

Some adventurers are not satisfied with just one incredible trip. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountains on every continent, biked across Canada, and run a long-distance race in the Sahara Desert in 45ºC heat. However, her most impressive journey was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and had to be rescued. While many would have given up at that moment, Meagan decided to continue. She reached the South Pole forty days later, pulling a sled with her tent and food through freezing temperatures and ice storms.

Blek le Rat started by painting rats on the walls of his hometown, Paris. Today, he aims to raise awareness about various social issues. He creates artworks of homeless individuals in large cities to encourage people to consider the problem of homelessness.

In certain areas, local councils have attempted to encourage artists to avoid painting graffiti randomly by providing designated spaces for their work. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can freely paint on walls. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city council has even permitted some graffiti artists to paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is an artist from Cape Town, South Africa. She creates large, colorful paintings of people and animals and enjoys discovering various locations. Her artwork can be seen on sidewalks, in abandoned factories, and on old cars. She appreciates that most street art is temporary and will eventually be removed by the weather or city cleaners. For her, this represents how life is full of changes, with cycles of endings and new beginnings.

In her previous job, Gabriela was accustomed to a culture with a high power distance, where people respect authority and everyone has a specific role. In that environment, leaders usually make the important decisions and are rarely questioned. On the other hand, her Swedish team was familiar with a low power distance culture, where employees often work together with their managers to find solutions and make decisions. In this setting, leaders take on a coaching role, promoting independent thinking and welcoming challenges.

When Gabriela recognized the cultural differences between herself and her team, she took the initiative to have an open discussion with them about their feelings regarding her leadership. Her team was pleased to be asked for their opinions and expressed that they were not accustomed to being told what to do. They appreciated having more freedom to take initiative and be creative. When Gabriela specified exactly what she needed them to do, they felt that she did not trust them to perform their jobs effectively. They understood that Gabriela took their attempts to challenge or change her decisions personally, and they were able to explain that this was simply how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos são irmãos gêmeos idênticos que vêm de São Paulo. Eles fazem pinturas que vão desde pequenas tags até enormes e coloridas imagens de pessoas nas laterais dos edifícios. Seu trabalho é muitas vezes tão grande que precisam de guindastes para conseguir pintar. Em 2007, eles cobriram todo um castelo na Escócia com suas pinturas.

Throughout history, people have painted and written on walls. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe created paintings of animals and humans in caves. Graffiti has been discovered on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists have uncovered many examples of graffiti written in Latin, which include religious, political, and romantic messages, as well as some magic spells!

Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? If so, you are not alone. Each year, thousands of people attempt to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. Unlike the explorers of the past who relied on maps and compasses, today’s adventurers use modern technology such as GPS and satellite phones. Many of these adventurers are passionate about nature and use their journeys to raise awareness about various environmental issues, while others aim to help those in need and raise funds for charities.

The first mission is DART, which stands for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. The plan is to test DART on the moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, known as 'Didymoon,' is 150 meters wide and orbits its larger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that the impact of DART will change Didymoon's orbit enough for telescopes on Earth to detect it.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. After losing her father in a mining accident, she must provide food for her family. She hunts in the woods around District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes skilled with a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is chosen as a tribute, Katniss volunteers to take her place. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss finds herself in a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details about them. Consider the people and places in your dreams, as they might add to their meaning. After a week, you might be surprised by how much you have written down. You can then start to connect your dreams to the events and feelings in your everyday life.

Historically, many bridges were built from wood, making them more likely to catch fire. This was especially common with old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could sometimes ignite a fire that would destroy the bridge.

It is difficult to predict how street art will evolve in the future, but we can see some trends emerging. Most street artists are young individuals who create art in their local areas, but an increasing number are traveling and working internationally. Additionally, many artists are using the internet to communicate and share images of their work. The art community is also beginning to acknowledge street art as a valid form of art. While we cannot foresee the future of street art, we can be confident that it will continue to exist.

Suzanne Collines has always found war news upsetting. As a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Although her mother tried to protect her by not discussing the war, she still watched news programs about it and knew her dad was involved. This was a very frightening experience for her.

A global survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) collected responses from over 40,000 millennials and non-millennials about workplace culture, communication, pay structure, career development, and work-life balance. In a different survey by Deloitte, more than 10,000 millennials participated to share their thoughts on the challenges and opportunities in the modern work environment.

Erik Weihenmayer, an adventurer from the United States, has ridden a bike through the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Remarkably, he has been blind since he was 13. In addition to his adventures, he encourages people with disabilities to lead active lives and organizes climbing trips for young blind people.

Online platforms are allowing people to make some extra money easily. For instance, busy parents might not have sold their children's old items at local markets before, but now they can sell barely used baby clothes and expensive baby gear online to get some money back.

Pi and Richard Parker spend 227 days in a lifeboat. They experience hunger, illness, and exhaustion. They face violent storms and the intense heat of the Pacific sun, but they somehow manage to survive. At times, Pi finds comfort in his three religions, but at other times, he feels lonely and hopeless. Eventually, they see the Mexican coast on the horizon, and everything changes. I won’t spoil the ending, so you should read the book to discover what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they reach land.

Chloe got home from school, made herself a cup of coffee, and took it to her bedroom. Although she had some homework to finish, she decided to wait and enjoy the quiet hour before her parents returned. She liked this time because the house would soon be filled with the sounds of conversation, the TV, or her dad listening to jazz while preparing dinner. It was also a good time for her to play with her pet rats.

In 2010, the planetary defense team at NASA identified and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1 kilometer wide. These 'near-Earth objects' are the size of mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's orbit. NASA estimates that there are about 50 more to log, but states that none of the 887 known asteroids pose a significant danger to our planet.

After deciding to go to school, Auggie faces his first day, which makes him very anxious like any child starting at a new school. However, because of his appearance, it becomes a painful experience. Other kids avoid sitting next to him, and he notices them staring or whispering about him. Fortunately, he becomes friends with Jack and Summer, who he talks to at lunch. But the challenges don’t end with the first day. Auggie soon discovers that some classmates are afraid to touch him because they think he has 'the plague.' As the school year goes on, Auggie experiences many emotional highs and lows, and a shocking event at a school camp changes everything for him.

The two men gazed toward the northern side of the property, which seemed to stretch endlessly. The fences were almost invisible from their position. A bored teenage boy wouldn't be able to escape on foot. Sam observed the largest horse, kicking the ground with its heavy hooves. He wondered if the boy could ride. A skilled rider could easily find trouble out here, far from anyone else. However, someone who knew nothing about horses might face even greater trouble trying to get away from his father.

Over 4,000 climbers, aged between thirteen and eighty, have successfully reached the summit of Everest. Although climbing high mountains in freezing temperatures and severe storms remains very dangerous, the world's top climbers are now seeking new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria developed a passion for mountain climbing as a teenager. After she graduated from school, she worked as a nurse while still climbing in her spare time.

After successfully climbing Everest, Gerlinde decided to take on the challenge of climbing all fourteen of the world's 8,000-meter peaks. To make it even more difficult, she climbs without using oxygen tanks, which is risky because low oxygen levels can affect how the brain and body work. Gerlinde also uses her fame as a climber to support a charity that helps poor children and orphans in Nepal.

When we think about the things we have bought over the years, we can see that not everything is being used properly: the thick coat we thought was fashionable even though we live in a tropical country, the smartphone we stopped using after getting the latest model, the car that we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that has turned into a storeroom.

Throughout history and in different cultures, dreams have been linked to prophecy. People believed that dreams were messages from the gods meant to provide knowledge or insight. Even today, many people can remember a time when they dreamed about an event, place, or person, and later that dream came true.

Some of the largest and most expensive transportation projects globally have involved the construction of bridges. Bridges serve as essential connections that enable cars, trucks, and trains to travel over water, mountain gorges, or other roads.

After weeks of frustration, Gabriela sent an email to her Swedish manager about the problems she was having with her team. Her manager only asked if she believed her team was still performing well and what could help her collaborate better with them. Gabriela found her manager to be vague and felt he was not managing the situation effectively.

Dogs that live in packs have learned that humans tend to give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to beg for food for the entire pack. Some dogs have even figured out how to use the metro system to travel around the city! Scientists are unsure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One theory is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of their favorite places. Another possibility is that they have learned to recognize the names of the stations from the announcements. Regardless, metro passengers have become so accustomed to seeing dogs on the trains that they often go unnoticed by locals.

Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk the entire length of the Amazon River. He started at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and arrived at the river's mouth in Brazil after two years and four months, having walked 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest is home to dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, which meant Ed was often in danger. Luckily, he survived with just a few thousand bites from mosquitoes and ants.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes every year, which is around four percent of their income. While this might not seem like a lot, it reveals two more serious issues for society and the environment. First, a large part of this spending is done using credit cards. Currently, British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of their average clothing budget. Additionally, people are not only spending money they don’t have, but they are also buying things they don’t really need. Britain discards 300,000 tons of clothing each year, most of which goes to landfills.

Ed's walk would have been impossible without technology. He used a radio to ask the rainforest people for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to meet him and helped guide him through the hardest parts of the journey. As he walked, Ed wrote a blog to share his daily experiences. He used the media interest in his trip to raise awareness about the destruction of the rainforest and to collect money for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have recognized the profit potential of the sharing economy and are trying to benefit from underused resources. A popular business model involves companies providing online platforms that connect customers with those who can offer certain products or services. For instance, Airbnb serves as a middleman, allowing people to rent out their unused rooms and houses for extra income. Similarly, Uber encourages individuals to use their personal cars as taxis to earn additional money during their free time.

One of the key roles of modern zoos is to support international breeding programs for endangered species. In the wild, some of the rarest animals struggle to find mates and reproduce, and they also face threats from poachers, habitat loss, and predators. A good zoo provides a safe environment for these species to live and breed. Additionally, as the numbers of certain wild species decline, there is a greater risk of their populations becoming too genetically similar. Breeding programs act as a safeguard by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild, which helps increase genetic diversity.

Both types of accidents are quite rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to collapse for different reasons. Trains can bring down a bridge due to the force of their impact, while boats can cause a collapse because of their large weight, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to prevent bridge failures is to plan for them. Modern technologies that detect structural weaknesses, safer working conditions, and improved designs can all help reduce these serious accidents.

At first, Pi is afraid of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers that there are hungry sharks in the water and realizes he has to climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other until only Pi and the tiger remain. Fortunately for Pi, the tiger, whom he names Richard Parker, is seasick and is not interested in eating him at that moment.

When Pi turns 16, a new government is elected that his parents do not support. Concerned about what will happen next, Pi's parents decide to shut down the zoo and move to Canada. They sell some of the animals to zoos in North America and travel by ship to Canada with the remaining animals. Unfortunately, a terrible storm occurs, and the ship sinks. Tragically, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi finds himself in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a large tiger.

The Hunger Games is a highly successful book for teenagers and young adults written by American author Suzanne Collins. Since its release in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies globally. It was also the first book aimed at young readers to sell more than a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games has been adapted into a major Hollywood film, which has also been very successful, earning 152.5 million dollars in its opening weekend in North America alone!

Dreams could be a way for our mind to organize the thoughts we have during the day, but they often have symbolic meanings. When we are awake, our thoughts usually come to us as words, like conversations we have in our heads. However, when we sleep, the part of our brain that controls language becomes less active, while the part that manages emotions becomes more active.

Good relationships are a key part of being happy. A study showed that most happy people have strong connections with friends and family and make time to be with them regularly. It’s also important to have at least one person to talk to about personal feelings, which is called 'self-disclosure.' Just one close friend is enough, along with a network of other relationships. Having many friends to do activities with or chat about music or football isn’t enough; that deeper connection is essential. Some people need to improve their listening skills to create stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck discussed how the brain can change and how we can develop skills and talents that we may not have had at first. Many people usually give praise based on the final results and natural abilities, such as saying, "You have a great eye for details" or "You are really talented at organizing events." However, studies suggest that by focusing on the process—like praising effort, experimentation, and problem-solving—we can encourage the growth of new skills and the improvement of existing talents.

The rover periodically analyzes the air around it, and in 2014, it discovered methane, a basic organic molecule and a key component of natural gas. Methane only lasts for a few hundred years, which suggests that something on Mars is producing more of it. According to NASA, Mars emits thousands of tons of methane at a time, and the levels of methane fluctuate with the seasons, almost as if the planet is breathing.

Early in her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave a group of ten-year-olds problems that were slightly too difficult for them. One group responded positively, saying they enjoyed the challenge and believed they could develop their abilities. Dweck described this as a 'growth mindset,' where they focused on what they could achieve in the future. However, another group of children felt that their intelligence was being judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and struggled to imagine how they could improve. Some of these children mentioned they might cheat in the future, while others looked for someone who performed worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films often take place in uninhabited locations, such as abandoned hospitals, creepy empty houses, or ghost towns. There is something intriguing about these lonely places. What was life like when people lived there? Why did they leave? The silence in these places can also be very frightening. Additionally, abandoned locations are useful for horror film directors because it makes sense that there would be no phone coverage there.

Regardless of the type of house, basements are always scary in horror films. They are often where something is hiding or where the villain keeps their tools. Basements tend to be dark and damp, and you can only access them through a narrow staircase. They always feel creepy, even if there is nothing down there.

Gary Collins, an off-duty police officer, was watching the London riots on television when he recognized several individuals. He cut his holiday short to assist with their identification. Over six months, he reviewed CCTV footage and managed to identify 190 people, often just by looking at their eyes. His contribution was crucial to the investigation, especially since facial recognition software could only identify one person out of 200,000 hours of footage.

I think it's fascinating to think about how we can speed up our evolution by improving our bodies. Imagine if we could implant a computer in our brains! Soon, we might be able to do this and enhance our math skills, audiovisual perception, and memory. This idea will become more common in the future.

The talk was really interesting, and the speaker made some important points. For example, how can we expect teenagers to avoid texting during homework when they see their parents posting on social media while cooking or waiting at a stoplight? She also pointed out that people often want to be in multiple places at once, switching between real-life conversations and online chats. I see this with my teenage daughter and her friends; they meet up but often sit in silence while each is engaged in a different online conversation.

While some news stories suggest that the world is becoming more violent, there is also some reason to be hopeful. Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that resulted in over 100,000 deaths. Today, although there are still civil wars, countries are generally co-existing more peacefully than in the past. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. On a positive note, even though deaths from violent crime are nine times more likely than those from political conflict, the global murder rate has slightly decreased, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has devoted her life to supporting human rights and has witnessed many international projects in her country aimed at educating and training women and girls. Unfortunately, when these projects end, the women are often left with nothing. Realizing that Bangladesh needed to assert itself, she combined her passions for mountaineering and human rights to change attitudes towards women in her country. She began climbing while working on humanitarian campaigns in Tibet and Nepal, as most people in the flat coastal country of Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign appears to be effective, as people in her country and around the world are starting to take notice.

Many people believe that developing countries are in a bad situation, facing extreme poverty, ruled by dictators, and lacking hope for change. However, this is not accurate. In reality, a significant transformation is taking place. Over the past 20 years, more than 700 million people have improved their income and lifted themselves out of poverty. Additionally, six million fewer children die from diseases each year, millions more girls are attending school, and many people now have access to clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback more positive by placing a negative comment between two positive ones. However, if this becomes a habit, employees may start to see positive feedback as just a way to cover up the negatives, which reduces its importance. Instead, positive feedback should be given to truly support and motivate good performance.

I am a member of a group that aims to stop killer robots. Forget the scary image of a robot from movies; right now, military machines like drones and sentry robots are already being used to kill with minimal human involvement.
